hookLine: Two bills came to one house. Pay or face termination. Mary Craft telephoned after a final notice and said she had paid a bill.

OP.primary: MEMPHIS LIGHT, GAS & WATER DIVISION v. CRAFT
OP.secondary: 436 U. S. 1 — argued November 1977, decided 1 May 1978

ACT_1.secondary: October 1972. They move in. The house had been used previously as a duplex.

ACT_1.label: Separate sets of gas and electric meters serving one household, and one water meter. The seller said the second set was inoperative.

ACT_1.secondary: A meter reader tells them both sets are running. They hire a private plumber and electrical contractor themselves.

ACT_1.quote: Because the contractor did not consolidate the meters properly, a condition of which the Crafts were not aware, they continued to receive two bills until January 1974.
ACT_1.attribution: Memphis Light, Gas & Water Div. v. Craft, 436 U. S. 1 (1978) — the body of the opinion

ACT_1.primary: A SECOND ACCOUNT, IN A FOOTNOTE
ACT_1.secondary: The Court quotes the brief filed by the Crafts' own lawyers

ACT_1.quote: Not until after the action was filed were the Crafts able to discover that they continued to receive double computer billings because MLG&W failed to combine the two accounts properly
ACT_1.attribution: The same opinion, n. 7 — quoting Brief for Respondents 5

ACT_1.label: Terminations during this period, as the majority counts them. No month, no duration, no season, no figure for any bill behind them.

ACT_1.quote: Mrs. Craft sought in good faith to determine the cause of the "double billing," but was unable to obtain a satisfactory explanation or any suggestion for further recourse from MLG&W employees.
ACT_1.attribution: The District Court's finding, quoted by the Court
The District Court, on her telephone call after a final notice

ACT_1.quote: The procedure for an opportunity to talk with management was not adequately explained to Mrs. Craft, although she repeatedly tried to get some explanation for the problems of two bills and possible duplicate charges.
ACT_1.attribution: The District Court, quoted by the Court (Pet. for Cert. 38-39)

ACT_1.quote: an employee of uncertain authority told Mrs. Craft, apparently without explanation or attempt at investigation, "[w]ell, you have to pay on the other" bill
ACT_1.attribution: Memphis Light, Gas & Water Div. v. Craft (1978), n. 19 — citing App. 91

ACT_1.secondary: They file in the District Court for the Western District of Tennessee

ACT_2.secondary: As the District Court set it out. This is the clock the family on Alaska Street was living on.

events.text: A bill is mailed to the service location
The last day to pay the net amount
The meter reader terminates electric service

ACT_2.quote: Electric service is then terminated by the meter reader, unless the customer assures him that payment is in the mail, shows a paid receipt, or explains that nonpayment was due to illness.
ACT_2.attribution: The District Court's description of the utility's practice, n. 4

ACT_2.label: Days, at least, between the mailing of the bill and the actual termination of service
Delinquent cutoffs, September 1973 through February 1974 — the dissent's figure

ACT_2.secondary: A prominent legend on the notices, the dissent says. Calls answered by 30 or 40 employees, each empowered to delay a cutoff for three days.
Credit counselors · the chief clerk · the supervisor in credit and collection · the Board of Commissioners. A customer may be accompanied by an appropriate representative.
March 1973. The trial judge called it a generous program: half a past due bill, the balance over the next three. The plaintiffs were participants in it.

ACT_2.quote: the MLG&W notice only warn[ed] the customer to pay or face termination.
ACT_2.attribution: The Court of Appeals, 534 F. 2d 684, 688-689 — quoted by the Court

ACT_2.label: Of the utility's customers, about, got the flyer that made no mention of a procedure for a disputed claim. Which flyer reached Alaska Street the record does not establish.

ACT_2.quote: if there is any dispute concerning the amount due, bring your bill to the office at . . ., or phone . . . .
ACT_2.attribution: The other flyer — quoted by the Court from 534 F. 2d 684, 688 n. 4

ACT_2.label: High bill complaints processed in 1973, on the secretary-treasurer's testimony

ACT_2.primary: THE RULE THAT DID NOT APPLY
ACT_2.secondary: Tennessee required posted rules on the adjustment of complaints — for an independent utility district, as opposed to a utility division of a municipality

items.label: Plaintiffs the trial court found substantially deprived
Plaintiffs named as the possible exception

ACT_3.attribution: The trial judge's own word, in quotation marks in the opinion

ACT_3.label: The credit the trial judge hoped would be issued

ACT_3.quote: terminations which should have been unnecessary had effectual relief been afforded them as requested
ACT_3.attribution: The trial judge, in the same decision that gave judgment to the utility

ACT_3.secondary: By an order filed 30 December 1974 the court noted the credit had been issued and some new procedures instituted

ACT_3.quote: [o]f the balance claimed by MLG&W in March, 1974, some involved possible gas overcharges and double or duplicate billings with respect to city service fees.
ACT_3.attribution: The District Court, quoted by the Court, n. 8

ACT_3.quote: The trial judge evidently accepted the Division's claim that it was engaged in "split billing" rather than "double billing."

ACT_3.label: The monthly city service fee, charged on each set of meters — the dissent's figure

items.label: Courts that decided whether the money was owed

ACT_3.quote: The validity of the damages claim is a matter for initial determination by the courts below.
ACT_3.attribution: Memphis Light, Gas & Water Div. v. Craft (1978), n. 8

ACT_3.secondary: The refusal to certify was affirmed. What follows is a judgment about two people at one address.
Notice that a disputed bill can be challenged · an established procedure for resolving it. Certiorari granted 22 February 1977.

ACT_3.quote: respondents no longer desire a hearing to resolve a continuing dispute over their bills, as the double-meter problem has been clarified during this litigation
ACT_3.attribution: The Court, on why the case nearly went away

ACT_3.quote: Respondents' claim for actual and punitive damages arising from MLG&W's terminations of service saves this cause from the bar of mootness.
ACT_3.attribution: Memphis Light, Gas & Water Div. v. Craft (1978), Part II

ACT_4.quote: An exception to the general rule exists when the customer has a bona fide dispute concerning the correctness of the bill.
ACT_4.attribution: Trigg v. Middle Tennessee Electric Membership Corp. (Tenn. App. 1975), quoted in Craft

ACT_4.quote: A public utility should not be able to coerce a customer to pay a disputed claim.
ACT_4.attribution: Trigg, quoted in Craft — rejecting the utility's own rulebook

ACT_4.quote: notice reasonably calculated, under all the circumstances, to apprise interested parties of the pendency of the action and afford them an opportunity to present their objections
ACT_4.attribution: Mullane v. Central Hanover Trust Co., 339 U. S. 306, 314 (1950) — notice to the beneficiaries of a trust fund, quoted in Craft

items.label: Told the customer the thing was about to happen
Told the customer there was somewhere to object

ACT_4.quote: In essence, recipients of a cutoff notice should be told where, during which hours of the day, and before whom disputed bills appropriately may be considered.
ACT_4.attribution: Memphis Light, Gas & Water Div. v. Craft (1978), n. 15

ACT_4.secondary: Not a judge, not a hearing officer, not a lawyer. Designated personnel duly authorized to review disputed bills with complaining customers and to correct any errors.

ACT_4.quote: Whether or not such a procedure may be available to other MLG&W customers, both courts below found that it was not made available to Mrs. Craft.
ACT_4.attribution: Memphis Light, Gas & Water Div. v. Craft (1978), Part IV-B

ACT_4.quote: Utility service is a necessity of modern life; indeed, the discontinuance of water or heating for even short periods of time may threaten health and safety. And the risk of an erroneous deprivation, given the necessary reliance on computers, is not insubstantial.
ACT_4.attribution: The Court, weighing the private interest and the risk of error

ACT_4.secondary: Sue for an injunction before the cutoff · sue for damages after it · pay and sue for a refund

ACT_4.quote: Although utility service may be restored ultimately, the cessation of essential services for any appreciable time works a uniquely final deprivation.
ACT_4.attribution: The Court, on why a lawsuit afterwards is not the same thing

ACT_4.quote: sums of money too small to justify engaging counsel or bringing a lawsuit
ACT_4.attribution: The Court, answering the argument that the courts were open

ACT_4.label: Half the disputed bill, up front, to go on arguing

ACT_5.label: Services ordered restored, cutoffs enjoined, or dollars awarded

ACT_5.quote: The public utility enjoys a broad discretion in the scheduling and structuring of this "hearing," provided that the customer is afforded adequate time for effective presentation of his complaint prior to termination.
ACT_5.attribution: Memphis Light, Gas & Water Div. v. Craft (1978), n. 22

ACT_5.quote: I have no quarrel with the Court's conclusion that as a matter of Tennessee law a customer has a legitimate claim of entitlement to continued utility services as long as the undisputed portions of his utility bills are paid.
ACT_5.attribution: Stevens, J., dissenting, joined by the Chief Justice and Justice Rehnquist

ACT_5.quote: In fact, the two accounts were independent; because the Crafts refused to pay the balance on the second account, the Division terminated their service on several occasions. The District Court expressly found that the Division sent a final notice before each termination.
The record therefore indicates that Mrs. Craft did meet with Division employees having adequate authority but simply failed to persuade any of them that there was any error in her bills.
She was told that she had to pay on the other account as well. … In other words, an official of the Division did resolve the Crafts' dispute, correctly as it turned out.
ACT_5.attribution: Stevens, J., dissenting, n. 7 — the same sentence the majority prints as a brush-off

ACT_5.quote: The dissent advances its own reading of the record in this case, but offers no justification for sidestepping the determinations made below.
ACT_5.attribution: The Court, answering the dissent, n. 19

ACT_5.quote: For a homeowner surely need not be told how to complain about an error in a utility bill
ACT_5.attribution: Stevens, J., dissenting — the sentence the majority answered in n. 15

ACT_5.quote: The Court's holding that the Division's notice was constitutionally defective rests on a paternalistic predicate that I cannot accept.

Lay consumers of electric service, the uninterrupted continuity of which is essential to health and safety, should be informed clearly of the availability of an opportunity to present their complaint.
ACT_5.attribution: The Court, n. 15 — answering the dissent

ACT_5.quote: Although the Division's terminations number about 2,000 each month, the record does not reveal any actual case of harm to health or safety. The District Court found that the Division does not discontinue service when there is illness in a home.
These justifications suggest that the Court's new rule is the product of a policy determination rather than a traditional construction of the Constitution.
I do not believe the Constitution requires the State to employ procedures that are so simple that every lay person can always act effectively without the assistance of counsel.
ACT_5.attribution: Stevens, J., dissenting — the closing line before "I respectfully dissent."

items.label: Accounts of whose mistake it was, printed in the same opinion
Times the Court resolved which one was right

ENDING.label: Courts that decided whether the money was owed
High bill complaints in one year, and no description of the procedure ever distributed to customers

ENDING.quote: And petitioners would retain the option to terminate service after affording this opportunity and concluding that the amount billed was justly due.
ENDING.attribution: Memphis Light, Gas & Water Div. v. Craft, 436 U. S. 1 (1978)

_notes.script: episodes/_planning/EP64_memphis_script.en.v002.md is the confirmed script. It was CUT on 2026-08-06 after the real narration master measured over the ceiling; do not restore anything from an earlier revision.
_notes.runtime: MEASURED, not modelled: the ffprobed ElevenLabs master gives 1915.1s for 5105 narration words, inside the contract band [1620,1920]. The scripts' own 176 words-per-finished-minute model runs 8-10 percent optimistic and is what put two films on this slate over the ceiling. Re-ffprobe after any script edit and check against 1920 before committing anything downstream.
_notes.voice: Pinned in the gen_narration_case.py registry and recorded in 06_audio/voice_plan.v001.json: voice nPczCjzI2devNBz1zQrb, model eleven_multilingual_v2, stability 0.35, similarity_boost 0.80. Do not change them: they are what makes these four episodes comparable to each other.
_notes.figures: 101 beats from EP64_memphis_beats.v002.json. USE v002, NOT v001. v001 carried non-verbatim quotations, wrong attributions and, on two episodes, a kind the builder rejects outright, and it spent the slot at figures[-1] -- which build_figures overwrites with the AI-disclosure card -- on the film's closing line.
_notes.people_plates: 10 declared in episode_spec as people_plates. They are named with this episode's prefix, not P###; check_episode_inputs reads the declared list.
_notes.mandatory_stills: episode_spec declares 215. The THUMB plates are deliberately excluded: a thumbnail is packaging, not a cut, and check_spec_satisfied fails any declared still that is in no cut.
_notes.assets: BLOCKER: only 16 archive clips survived visual QC against a floor near 146 for a film this long, and there are no motion clips at all. greene solved the same problem with 122 i2v clips in remotion/public/greene/motion; the tool that made them is not in this repository. The asset_manifest this config points at cannot be built until that pool exists.
_notes.shotlist: Do not hand-write one. It was retired at EP38. scripts/build_case_film_generic.py --config <this file> generates it.
